## 1. Purpose

This SOP describes the deployment and operation of static (closed,
non-flow-through) chambers for manual measurement of soil CO~2~ efflux
in the field. Static chambers are a simple, low-cost method for
quantifying soil respiration across treatments, land uses, or seasonal
gradients when the Picarro CRDS automated system
([SOP-F504](SOP-F504-picarro-field-deployment.qmd)) is not available
or when additional spatial replication is needed. The method captures
headspace gas samples at timed intervals, which are analyzed for CO~2~
concentration using a portable infrared gas analyzer (IRGA), syringe
samples returned to the lab, or soda-lime traps.


## 2. Scope

- **Applies to:** Manual static chamber measurements of soil CO~2~
  efflux at EA Program field sites; applicable to grasslands,
  agricultural plots, restoration sites, and forest soils
- **Does not apply to:** Automated dynamic chambers with the Picarro
  CRDS analyzer (see [SOP-F504](SOP-F504-picarro-field-deployment.qmd));
  eddy covariance or gradient flux methods; aquatic CO~2~ flux
  measurements; N~2~O or CH~4~ flux measurements requiring GC or CRDS
  analysis (though the same chambers can be used with different
  analytical endpoints)
- **Location:** All EA Program terrestrial field sites


## 3. Responsibilities

| Role              | Responsibility                                          |
|:------------------|:--------------------------------------------------------|
| PI / Field Lead   | Approve chamber design and deployment plan              |
| Trained Personnel | Install collars, deploy chambers, collect gas samples   |
| New Students      | Complete training before independent use                |


## 4. Safety and Hazards

::: {.callout-warning}
### Hazards

- **Physical:** Driving collars into soil with a mallet poses impact
  injury risk. Carrying chambers and equipment over uneven terrain.
- **Heat:** Southern California field sites can exceed 40 C. Metal
  chambers become extremely hot in direct sunlight; handle with gloves.
- **Chemical:** Soda-lime (NaOH/Ca(OH)~2~) is corrosive and causes
  burns on skin and eye contact. Concentrated NaOH solutions used for
  soda-lime traps are hazardous. Handle with gloves and safety glasses.
:::

### Required PPE

- [ ] Closed-toed shoes or field boots
- [ ] Nitrile gloves (required when handling soda-lime)
- [ ] Safety glasses (required when handling soda-lime or NaOH)
- [ ] Sun protection (hat, sunscreen)
- [ ] Work gloves (when driving collars)

### Emergency Procedures

For soda-lime or NaOH contact with skin or eyes, flush with clean
water for at least 15 minutes. Refer to
[SOP-F001 Field Safety](SOP-F001-field-safety.qmd) and
[SOP-L003 Hazardous Materials Handling](../lab_sops/SOP-L003-hazardous-materials-handling.qmd).


## 5. Equipment and Materials

### Chamber Components

| Item                                  | Notes                                    |
|:--------------------------------------|:-----------------------------------------|
| PVC soil collars (20--30 cm diameter, 10--15 cm tall) | Installed 24+ hours before first measurement |
| PVC chamber tops (opaque, with rubber gasket) | Must seal against collar; include a sampling port and a vent tube |
| Rubber gasket or closed-cell foam     | For airtight seal between collar and top |
| Vent tube (small-diameter tubing, 30--50 cm) | Equilibrates internal and atmospheric pressure without mass flow |
| Sampling port with septum             | For syringe sampling of headspace gas    |
| Reflective tape or insulation (optional) | To minimize solar heating of the chamber headspace |

### Gas Sampling (Syringe Method)

| Item                                  | Notes                                    |
|:--------------------------------------|:-----------------------------------------|
| Gas-tight syringes (20 or 60 mL)      | Luer-lock with stopcock                  |
| Pre-evacuated vials (Exetainer, 12 mL) | For storing gas samples for lab analysis |
| Needles (22 gauge)                    | For piercing septa                       |
| Portable IRGA (e.g., LI-COR LI-830 or PP Systems EGM-5) | Optional; provides real-time CO~2~ readings |

### Soda-Lime Method (Alternative)

| Item                                  | Notes                                    |
|:--------------------------------------|:-----------------------------------------|
| Soda-lime granules (indicating grade) | Weighed pre- and post-deployment         |
| Glass jars with lids                  | For containing soda-lime during deployment |
| Analytical balance (0.01 g)           | For pre- and post-weighing               |
| Desiccator                            | For equilibrating soda-lime moisture     |

### General

| Item                                  | Notes                                    |
|:--------------------------------------|:-----------------------------------------|
| Stopwatch or timer                    | For timed gas sampling intervals         |
| Thermometer (soil and air)            | For recording temperature during deployment |
| Soil moisture probe or TDR (optional) | For recording volumetric moisture        |
| Mallet or dead-blow hammer            | For driving collars into soil            |
| Measuring tape and ruler              | For measuring collar insertion depth and headspace height |
| Field notebook                        | For recording all metadata               |


## 6. Procedure

### 6.1 Collar Installation

Install collars at least 24 hours before the first measurement to
allow the soil disturbance from insertion to subside.

1. Select collar locations according to the experimental design
   (randomized, stratified, etc.; see
   [SOP-F005](SOP-F005-random-sampling-design.qmd)).
2. Clear surface litter from a circular area slightly larger than the
   collar diameter.
3. Place the collar on the soil surface and press gently to mark the
   insertion point.
4. Using the mallet and a wooden block placed on top of the collar,
   drive the collar into the soil to a depth of 3--5 cm. Avoid driving
   deeper than 5 cm, as this severs a disproportionate fraction of
   surface roots and alters the flux.
5. Measure and record the collar insertion depth and the height of the
   collar rim above the soil surface (this determines the headspace
   volume).
6. Record the collar ID and GPS coordinates per
   [SOP-F006](SOP-F006-gps-site-navigation.qmd).

### 6.2 Syringe Sampling Method

1. Record ambient air temperature and soil temperature (at 5 cm depth
   adjacent to the collar).
2. Place the chamber top on the collar. Ensure the gasket creates a
   tight seal. Note the deployment time (T~0~).
3. Immediately take a T~0~ headspace sample: insert the syringe needle
   through the sampling septum, pump the syringe 3 times to mix the
   headspace, then withdraw the sample volume. Close the stopcock.
   Transfer to a pre-evacuated Exetainer vial by puncturing the vial
   septum.
4. Repeat sampling at regular intervals. A typical schedule is T~0~,
   T~10~, T~20~, and T~30~ (minutes). For high-flux soils, use shorter
   intervals (e.g., 0, 5, 10, 15 min).
5. After the final sample, remove the chamber top and record the time.
6. Label each Exetainer with the collar ID, date, and time point.
7. Store vials at room temperature and analyze within 48 hours by GC
   or IRGA.

### 6.3 Portable IRGA Method (Real-Time)

If a portable IRGA is available:

1. Connect the IRGA inlet to the chamber sampling port via tubing.
2. Deploy the chamber and record CO~2~ concentration continuously or
   at 1-minute intervals for 5--10 minutes.
3. The flux is calculated from the linear increase in CO~2~
   concentration over time.

### 6.4 Soda-Lime Method (24-Hour Deployment)

1. Pre-dry soda-lime granules at 105 C for 2 hours, cool in a
   desiccator, and weigh to 0.01 g. Record the initial mass.
2. Place 20--30 g of soda-lime in an open glass jar inside the collar.
3. Seal the chamber top onto the collar. Deploy for 24 hours.
4. Include at least two "blank" chambers: sealed chambers with
   soda-lime but placed on an impermeable surface (plastic sheeting)
   to measure handling and atmospheric absorption artifacts.
5. After 24 hours, remove the jar, cap it, and return to the lab.
6. Dry the soda-lime at 105 C for 2 hours, cool, and reweigh.
7. Calculate CO~2~ absorbed as the mass gain, correcting for the
   blank.

::: {.callout-note}
The soda-lime method provides an integrated 24-hour flux estimate but
is less precise than syringe or IRGA methods. It is best suited for
comparative studies (e.g., treatment vs. control) rather than absolute
flux quantification.
:::


## 7. Flux Calculation

For the syringe or IRGA method, calculate the flux using:

$$
F = \frac{\Delta C}{\Delta t} \times \frac{V}{A} \times \frac{P}{R \times T}
$$

where:

- $F$ = CO~2~ flux (umol m^-2^ s^-1^)
- $\Delta C / \Delta t$ = rate of change of CO~2~ concentration in the
  headspace (ppm s^-1^), from the slope of a linear regression of
  concentration vs. time
- $V$ = headspace volume (m^3^) = collar area $\times$ headspace height
- $A$ = collar area (m^2^)
- $P$ = atmospheric pressure (Pa)
- $R$ = universal gas constant (8.314 J mol^-1^ K^-1^)
- $T$ = air temperature (K)

If the concentration increase is nonlinear, a nonlinear (e.g.,
Hutchinson-Mosier) model may provide a better flux estimate. Consult
the PI.


## 8. Quality Control

- Deploy at least 3 replicate chambers per treatment or plot.
- Include at least one "blank" chamber per sampling event (chamber
  sealed on an impermeable surface) to assess leakage and background.
- Inspect collar seals before each deployment. Soil settling or animal
  disturbance can break the seal.
- Record soil temperature and moisture alongside every flux
  measurement; these are the primary drivers of soil respiration.
- Reject any measurement where the R^2^ of the linear regression
  (concentration vs. time) is below 0.90, unless the flux is near
  zero.
- Avoid measuring during or immediately after rainfall, as water
  pooling on the collar disrupts gas exchange.

## 11. Training Record

Before deploying soil respiration chambers independently, personnel
must:

1. Read this SOP and [SOP-F504](SOP-F504-picarro-field-deployment.qmd)
   in full
2. Demonstrate proper collar installation and headspace volume
   measurement
3. Perform a supervised syringe sampling or IRGA measurement at one
   site
4. Calculate flux from field data and demonstrate agreement with the
   trainer's calculation
5. Be signed off by the PI or field lead
